title: Warmup Fidelity Shepherd: noise-aware attention kernel warmup and probabilistic fallback plan
creator: Liam Chen
notes: 2026-02-20: Ticket created to pilot a 'Warmup Fidelity Shepherd' that reduces attention-kernel oscillation during v2->v3 rollouts by scoring startup signals and applying probabilistic fallbacks.

2026-02-25: Spike complete — implemented a noise-aware fidelity score (F) computed from short-window p95 decode jitter, KV-cache hit rate, and microbatch padding fraction. Baseline F thresholds chosen empirically (0.6/0.8) from sample of 2k requests.

2026-03-01: Canary run on staging (10% of traffic) with softening coefficient alpha=0.25 reduced v3 switchbacks by ~62% but increased p95 latency for long-context (>8k) by +18ms. Logged delta to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/runtime/warmup-fidelity-742013

2026-03-03: Decision: keep soft approach — shepherd will prefer v3 when F>0.8, probe with single-token prober when 0.6<=F<=0.8, and fallback to v2 with probabilistic backoff when F<0.6. Backoff uses jittered exponential with base=1.5 and max=60s.

2026-03-04: Implementation notes: prefilling logic now includes per-shard KV priming for top-5 recent prefixes to reduce cold-cache tail. Added microbatch-padding-aware warmup to avoid biasing F during batched synthetic probes.

2026-03-06: Observability: added 'stability_budget' metric (0..1) that decays when model oscillation or decode errors occur. Alert threshold set to <0.4 for 1m window. Dash link and sample charts attached in attachments.

2026-03-08: Review feedback from SRE — request to add circuit-breaker that halts automatic rollouts after 3 consecutive customer-visible decode regressions. Action: add as follow-up sub-issue (ENG-742014).

2026-03-09: Performance profiling (GPU traces) indicates extra memcopies during v3 warmup on mixed-precision heads. Created short-term mitigation: pre-allocate warmup workspace and reuse across probes. Measured improvement: 9% reduction in warmup p50.

2026-03-10: Next steps: run extended canary (30% traffic) for 48h, coordinate with QA for synthetic jitter suite covering adversarial prefix sequences, and prepare release notes for runtime-1.22. Assigned follow-ups: SLO verification, PR review, and documentation updates.
